fullPassage: (A) The violin had always been Ann's thing since she was seven. Her teacher Mrs. Jones always said she had natural talent. But lately, every time Ann picked up her bow, she couldn't focus. She kept thinking about Victoria Gray, the brilliant violinist who had performed at Maestro Hall. Before the lesson with Mrs. Jones, Ann was watching Victoria's flawless technique on her smartphone, and it made (a) her chest feel tighter.  (B) That night, Ann deleted her social media app from her smartphone. She focused on practicing (b) her violin, trying to find herself, for a week. On Saturday, Ann picked up her violin and played a simple piece she'd known since childhood. Her music had mistakes, but it felt like her own music again. When she finished, her little sister Emma clapped enthusiastically. "When (c) you play, it makes the whole house feel nicer." Ann smiled, finally at peace.  (C) Hearing her words, Mrs. Jones smiled softly and said, "That's because you're measuring yourself against someone else's ruler. Comparison steals your joy and unique voice. Stop looking at (d) her journey and focus on your own." Hearing those comforting words, something profound shifted inside Ann. After the lesson, Ann took down Victoria Gray's picture that had always been on her bedroom wall.  (D) What was the point? Ann thought. I'll never be like her. As the lesson began, her teacher, Mrs. Jones, immediately noticed Ann's distraction. "Is everything alright, Ann?" asked Mrs. Jones. "I'm just wondering if I'm good enough to be special like Victoria," Ann said. "I used to love playing. Now (e) I just feel like I'm not good enough. title: Comparison Steals Your Joy
